basic_info.title: MTrajRec: Map-Constrained Trajectory Recovery via Seq2Seq Multi-task Learning
basic_info.venue: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining (KDD) 2021, pp. 1410-1419

method.critic_note: graph_integration downgraded to [uncertain] by critic-anti-drift (likely 'none'): RNTrajRec (ICDE'23) explicitly contrasts itself against prior recovery/matching work that 'ignore the topology of road network and only use grid information or raw GPS points' — which describes MTrajRec. Its encoder is GRU seq2seq + attention with a constraint-mask output layer, not a GNN road embedding.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: MTrajRec recovers fine-grained map-matched trajectories end-to-end with a GRU seq2seq encoder-decoder and a multi-task head that jointly predicts the road segment (classification) and the moving ratio (regression) under map constraints, but it uses an RNN rather than a transformer over a vectorized semantic graph, makes one-shot seq2seq predictions rather than RL decisions in a latent space, and is trained supervised on high-sampling-rate ground-truth trajectories rather than label-free on raw fleet GPS. No RDF/KG semantics are used.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Recovering dense, road-constrained trajectories from sparse/low-quality fleet GPS is highly relevant to BMW fleet analytics, but the supervised, RNN-based, label-dependent design diverges from the thesis's label-free transformer+latent-RL hybrid.
